message.content:
**Decision: Buy.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and placed one order.

**What I did and why:** Apple's latest annual report shows a business that is still growing modestly at scale with improving profitability: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), gross margin of $180.7B (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%), operating income of $123.2B (up from $114.3B), and operating cash flow of $118.3B. Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) only because of a one-time, non-cash-like $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision — pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5B from $113.7B, and the underlying operating trend is positive, led by Services (+13% to $96.2B) with iPhone roughly flat at $201.2B. The balance sheet remains very strong ($140.8B of cash and marketable securities, $95.0B of buybacks and $15.2B of dividends returned in FY2024), and the main watch items are Greater China weakness (−8% to $67.0B) and ongoing DMA/DOJ antitrust matters. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90 — about 0.1% above the market, so "close to current market" — for roughly $9,808, which is under the $10,000 per-order cap and brings today's total purchases to $9,808, well within the $20,000 daily limit. The order was a buy in an allowed name, required no transfer of funds out of the account, and filled at $222.90.
